I know this is old, but that doesn't seem very clear in the article. After going back to read it again, I still had to read those lines a few times, and I can kinda see that interpretation, but I think it could be worded better to reflect that guards, for instance, can hear the Keter's thoughts within 60m of the Keter once its blood is on an instance of SCP-721-1, while the Keter can hear whatever is nearby the device itself. I feel like there are several different SCiPs here all stored under one designation due only to similar appearance.

This was, indeed, three different articles at some point. They were, for the most part, being downvoted for not having enough meat to them on their own.

The main idea was that, getting one of these disks, you don't know whether you'll get a cool easy transcription device, a thing that you could use to prank people (or do other things with)… or get burnt to death.

Side note: When I did the rewrite/condensation/whatever, I decided that purifying someone's blood by burning tickled me a bit more than just going up in a pillar of flame.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: One problem: If this is used in containing sentient Keter SCPs, that means either A) A security guard is the subject and the Keter SCP (and all the other guards) can hear his thoughts, or B) That the Keter SCP is the subject and all guards can hear its thoughts, HOWEVER with practice it can hear the thoughts of all the guards and therefore a constant stalemate of actions and reactions would occur between the Guards and the Keter-level entity. I think it would be a horrible idea to allow Keter SCPs to read your thoughts (unless they can do that already). Furthermore, I'm pretty sure that a Keter-class that knew it was being "heard" might be able to project the most horrible image imaginable (given the abilities of most sentient Keter-classes, that's gonna be a lot more horrible than the most horrible thing a human can think of).
